t.1.92.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Pratīpa, devoted to the welfare of all beings, went to the bank of the Gaṅgā and sat there for many years, murmuring prayers.
t.1.92.3: As the royal sage was engaged in recitation, the spirited lady of divine form and lovely face came and sat upon his right thigh, which was like a śāla tree.
t.1.92.2: Gaṅgā, endowed with beauty and virtues, like Śrī in bodily form, her figure most enticing, rose up out of that water and came to him.
t.1.92.4: But King Pratīpa said to that spirited woman: "What pleasing thing shall I do for you, O fair lady, that is desired by you?"
t.1.92.5: I desire you, O king, best of the Kurus; accept me, for the rejection of women who are full of desire is condemned by the virtuous.
t.1.92.6: I would not out of desire approach another's wife, O fair-complexioned one, nor a woman not of my own class, O lovely lady; know that this is my righteous vow.
t.1.92.7: I am not unworthy, nor one who may not be approached, nor ever to be spoken ill of. Love me, O king, for I love you, a maiden and an excellent woman.
t.1.92.9: Having come to my right thigh, you have embraced me, O lovely lady; know, O timid one, that this is the seat of children and of daughters-in-law.
t.1.92.8: This pleasing thing to which you urge me is something I have set aside. Were I to consent otherwise, the violation of dharma would destroy me.
t.1.92.11: Be my daughter-in-law, O lovely one; I choose you for the sake of my son. For, O fair-thighed one, having come to me you have taken your place on the side of a daughter-in-law.
t.1.92.10: The left side is the place of a beloved woman, and that you have shunned; therefore I shall not act upon desire toward you, O woman of lovely limbs.
t.1.92.12: Let it be so, O knower of dharma; I shall be united with your son. Out of devotion to you alone shall I join the renowned Bhārata lineage.
t.1.92.14: He must not know my lineage, and whatever I may do, O lord, your son must never question any of it at all.
t.1.92.13: Of all the kings there are upon the earth, you are the supreme refuge; your virtues could not be told by me even in hundreds of years. Those of your lineage who have gone before, their goodness is unsurpassed.
t.1.92.16: Having said "So be it," she vanished right there, O king; and the king, awaiting the birth of a son, kept that in mind.
t.1.92.15: Dwelling thus with your son, I shall increase your joy, and through virtuous and beloved sons your son will attain heaven.
t.1.92.17: At that very time, O joy of the Kurus, Pratīpa, a bull among kṣatriyas, together with his wife, practised austerities for the sake of a son.
t.1.92.18: To those two, grown old, a son was born, he who had been Mahābhiṣa. He was born as the offspring of one who had become tranquil, and therefore he was Śaṃtanu.
t.1.92.19: And remembering the imperishable worlds he had won by his own deeds, Śaṃtanu was ever a doer of meritorious acts, O best of the Kurus.
t.1.92.20: Then Pratīpa instructed his son Śaṃtanu, who had reached youth: "Long ago, Śaṃtanu, a woman came to me for your welfare."
t.1.92.21: If that fair-complexioned woman, a divine lady full of longing and rich in beauty, should come to you in secret, my son, out of desire for a son, you must not question her: “Who are you, and whose are you, lovely woman?”
t.1.92.23: Having thus instructed his son Śaṃtanu, King Pratīpa then consecrated him in his own kingdom and entered the forest.
t.1.92.22: "Whatever she may do, O sinless one, you must not question her about that deed. At my command, love her as she loves you," so he said to him.
t.1.92.24: That wise king Śaṃtanu, renowned on earth as a bearer of the bow, became devoted to hunting and constantly roamed the forests.
t.1.92.25: Slaying deer and buffaloes, that best of kings wandered alone along the Gaṅgā, which was frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.
t.1.92.26: Once, great king, he saw a most excellent woman, blazing with beauty of form, like Śrī herself, the lotus-dwelling goddess, in visible form.
t.1.92.27: He saw her, flawless in every respect, with lovely teeth, adorned with divine ornaments, wearing a garment of fine cloth, alone, her radiance like the inner petals of a lotus.
t.1.92.29: And she, the charming woman, on merely seeing the king of great splendor roaming about, felt affection arise in her out of love, and could not be sated.
t.1.92.30: Then the king, soothing her with gentle words, said to her: "Whether you are a goddess or a Dānavī, a Gandharvī or an Apsaras...
t.1.92.28: Seeing her, the king's hair stood on end, and he was amazed at the richness of her beauty; as though drinking her in with his eyes, the lord of men could not be sated.
t.1.92.31: Whether you are a Yakṣī or a Pannagī or a human woman, O slender-waisted one, or whoever you may be, O you who shine like a child of the gods, become my wife, O lovely one!
t.1.92.32: Having heard these smiling, gentle and charming words of the king, and remembering her agreement with the Vasus, the blameless woman approached him.
t.1.92.33: And she spoke, gladdening the king's heart with her words: "I shall become your queen, O lord of the earth, obedient to your will."
t.1.92.34: But whatever I may do, O king, whether good or ill, I must not be stopped from it, nor must anything unpleasant be said to me.
t.1.92.35: For if you conduct yourself thus, O king, I will dwell with you; but if I am hindered or spoken to unkindly, I would leave you without a doubt.
t.1.92.36: Then, O best of the Bharatas, when the king had said "So be it" to her, she attained that best of kings and felt incomparable joy.
t.1.92.37: Having obtained her, Śaṃtanu, though self-controlled, enjoyed her as he desired; thinking, "She must not be questioned," he said nothing at all to her.
t.1.92.38: That lord of the earth was delighted by her good character and conduct, by the excellence of her beauty and nobility, and by the attentive service she gave him in private.
t.1.92.39: For she, the goddess Gaṅgā, the river that flows along three paths, was of divine form; that fair-complexioned lady had assumed a splendid human body.
t.1.92.40: She became as a wife at the side of Śaṃtanu, that lion among kings, whose splendor equaled that of the king of the gods, and whose desire had been fulfilled by good fortune.
t.1.92.42: Because of his attachment to love-making, that king, captivated by the virtues of that most excellent woman, did not notice the many years, seasons and months that had passed.
t.1.92.41: With her skill in lovemaking and tenderness, and with captivating amorous gestures and dances, she delighted the king, and just as she took delight, so too did he.
t.1.92.43: Delighting with her as he pleased, the lord of the people begot upon her eight sons who had the appearance of immortals.
t.1.92.44: And each son, as soon as he was born, she would cast into the water, O Bhārata; saying, "I please you," she drowned him in the stream of the Gaṅgā.
t.1.92.45: That was not pleasing then to King Śaṃtanu, yet the lord of the earth said nothing at all to her, for he was afraid of being abandoned.
t.1.92.46: Then, when the eighth son was born, the king, stricken with grief and wishing to save his own son, spoke to her, who seemed to be smiling.
t.1.92.47: "Do not kill! Who are you, and whose are you? Why do you slay our sons?" he said. "O slayer of sons, do not incur a very great sin; stop, O blameworthy one!"
t.1.92.49: I am Gaṅgā, the daughter of Jahnu, attended upon by hosts of great seers; I have dwelt with you in order to bring about the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods.
t.1.92.48: O you who long for a son, best of those blessed with sons, I will not kill your son. But this stay of mine with you has come to its end, just as the agreement was made.
t.1.92.50: These eight Vasus, gods of great fortune and great might, have come to human birth through the fault of Vasiṣṭha's curse.
t.1.92.51: Apart from you, no other begetter of them exists on earth, and there is no human woman here like me who could be their mother.
t.1.92.53: But this agreement was promised by me to the gods, the Vasus: "Each one as soon as he is born, I shall free from human birth."
t.1.92.52: Therefore, for the sake of becoming their mother, I came to the human state. By begetting the eight Vasus, you have won imperishable worlds.
t.1.92.54: Thus they have been freed from the curse of the great-souled Āpava. May it be well with you; I shall go. Protect this son of great vows.
t.1.92.55: This stay of mine with you, in its appointed turn, was arranged in the presence of the Vasus. Know this son, born of me, to be Gaṅgādatta, the one given by Gaṅgā.
